Prospective boundary — The Economics of Autonomous Work.

Before generating confirmation inputs, the 69-file protocol/source/oracle/analysis boundary is frozen at SHA-256 `41b8b56a39993e29dc313faa8633e36abd910872ab43e9a5dbe1ab2edc589407` (25 October 2026, 11:15:50 UTC). The 298,029-byte prospective checkpoint has been saved; ZIP SHA-256 `458bc2e65adeca9d69082b424c6951eaa0c363b5fab21777586013ae6be05127`.

Frozen design: one public source-inventory showcase (135 docs/assets records per version, development-selected), 36 fresh jobs (four reconciliation contexts × three difficulty levels × three instances; seed 2026102501), one source-linked exception summary using the released workbench, 108 repeated operating attempts across local process concurrency 1/2/4, and eight separately counted controls. Original released execution files remain unchanged. Independent Python CSV/SQLite acceptance requires complete exact records and source references; the common employer deadline is one eight-hour business day, distinct from a 30-second system safety cap.

Vincent's latest direction makes the economic comparison market-data-grounded: official labor rates and occupational tasks across Quebec, the United States and Europe, plus published historical human evidence with task/AI-use limitations. Recruitment is not a prerequisite. No matched human time or quality ratio will be invented; missing complete system costs remain null, and break-even/sensitivity inputs are explicit assumptions. Development failures and reviewer corrections are retained. No confirmation input or result has been produced at this notice. Existing release, publication and held Harness/Fleet decisions are unchanged.
